---
title: "04 · Categorical predictors"
subtitle: "Week 1"
---

::: {.guiding-q}
What if a predictor is a category?
:::

## In this session

- Dummy (treatment) coding and the reference level
- What the coefficients of a factor mean
- Other contrasts (sum coding) and when to use them
- Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons with `emmeans`

::: {.key-terms}
**Key terms:** [Contrasts and dummy coding](../../glossary.qmd#contrasts), [Reference level](../../glossary.qmd#reference-level), [Estimated marginal means](../../glossary.qmd#emmeans)
:::

## Learning goals

After this session you can

- explain how R turns a factor into numeric predictors,
- interpret coefficients relative to a reference level,
- obtain group means and contrasts with `emmeans`.

## Simulate first

```{r}
set.seed(4)
group <- factor(rep(c("control", "food", "toy"), each = 20))
mu    <- c(control = 10, food = 14, toy = 12)
y     <- rnorm(60, mu[group], 3)

m <- lm(y ~ group)
round(coef(m), 2)                       # intercept = control, others = differences
head(model.matrix(m)[c(1, 21, 41), ])   # the dummy variables behind the scenes
```
